bull_bear.body:
- Parentage of Waaree Energies Limited, one of India's largest solar PV module manufacturers, giving access to the Group's robust supply chain, procurement synergies, established customer relationships and brand equity
- Stated cost position: 'we operate with among the lowest production costs in the domestic PV industry'
- Pass-through clauses embedded in most orders plus order-backed procurement, so raw material price increases are largely passed on to customers
- Wide channel network and strong service capabilities supporting a favourable market position
- Multiple automated production lines with state-of-the-art stringing, layup, lamination, framing and testing equipment
- Customer advances against orders, which the Company says bolster liquidity
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material cost risk — Escalating raw material costs could weigh on solar photovoltaic products and affect future prospects; prices of key inputs such as polysilicon, aluminium and copper have been volatile. The Company relies on pass-through clauses embedded in most orders and order-backed procurement to pass increases on to customers.
- Competition risk — Intensifying competition presents a material risk to profitability; the Company counters with product certifications, a wide channel network, service capabilities and a low production-cost position.
- Liquidity risk — Liquidity can be hit by sudden shifts in demand or pricing, or by reliance on short-term financing. Mitigated by cash and cash equivalents, expected cash accruals over the next two fiscal years, and customer advances against orders.
- Working capital risk — An extended working capital cycle could increase borrowing needs to meet operational requirements; being addressed through tighter inventory management, improved receivables collection and evaluation of factoring or supply chain financing.
- Policy and regulatory risk — Changes in government policies and regulations affecting renewable energy, including subsidies, tax incentives or import/export restrictions, could affect demand for solar products and the Company's ability to grow its market presence.
- Skilled labour and contractor availability risk — Access to skilled employees and reliable contractors is essential to maintaining operational efficiency and executing supply orders smoothly; addressed via structured training programmes and long-standing contractor/supplier ties.
- Technology obsolescence risk — The fast pace of advancement in solar cell efficiency and module design means manufacturers must continually innovate to stay competitive; demand is shifting toward higher-efficiency formats such as bifacial and perovskite.
- No Risk Management Committee constituted — The Company was not required to constitute a Risk Management Committee during FY2025-26; risk oversight rests with the Directors, with the Audit Committee having additional oversight of financial risks and controls.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Indosolar manufactures high-efficiency solar photovoltaic modules, with a product portfolio spanning TOPCon and Mono PERC technology, from a single facility at Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh with installed module manufacturing capacity of 1.3 GW per annum. The facility runs multiple automated production lines with stringing, layup, lamination, framing and testing equipment. As a subsidiary of Waaree Energies Limited, the Company sells modules and renders job-work services to its holding company and is also securing orders from developers of power projects.

business.body: - Waaree Energies Limited — related party: Holding Company. Ordinary-course, arm's-length dealings during FY2025-26 comprised sale of solar modules/related goods, job work/services rendered, purchase of raw materials, purchase of finished goods, sale of manufacturing scrap, purchase of capital goods, and an unsecured loan availed from it. Several directors also hold directorships on its board.

business.body:
- Parentage of Waaree Energies Limited, one of India's largest solar PV module manufacturers, giving access to the Group's robust supply chain, procurement synergies, established customer relationships and brand equity
- Stated cost position: 'we operate with among the lowest production costs in the domestic PV industry'
- Pass-through clauses embedded in most orders plus order-backed procurement, so raw material price increases are largely passed on to customers
- Wide channel network and strong service capabilities supporting a favourable market position
- Multiple automated production lines with state-of-the-art stringing, layup, lamination, framing and testing equipment
- Customer advances against orders, which the Company says bolster liquidity
business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Strategic sourcing of key inputs such as silicon wafers and glass at competitive prices, pursuing both domestic and international sourcing avenues
- Build a diversified supplier base to reduce dependence on any single supplier and cushion against supply chain disruptions
- Deploy robust inventory control systems to cut wastage and ensure timely material availability for production
- Apply lean manufacturing principles and maintain standard operating procedures across all manufacturing processes
- Run a quality assurance framework across every stage of manufacturing and maintain compliance with applicable international and national quality standards (e.g. IEC, BIS)
- Cost optimisation: lower production costs, use resources efficiently and control overheads
- Working capital management to maintain cash flow for operations, timely supplier payments and debt obligations, with tighter inventory management and improved receivables collection to shorten the working capital cycle
- Evaluate alternative financing options such as factoring or supply chain financing to reduce reliance on borrowings
- Human resource development: talent acquisition across engineering, production, quality control and management, structured training, and retention through competitive compensation and career growth
- Manage input-cost exposure through pass-through clauses embedded in most orders and order-backed procurement practices
- No dividend has been declared, and consequently the Company has no dividend distribution policy in place.
- CSR provisions became applicable for the first time in FY2025-26 on the back of the Company's financial performance; the Board constituted a CSR Committee under Section 135 and the Company incurred CSR expenditure of approximately Rs. 22.00 Lakhs during the year, with the CSR Policy published on its website.
- The Company states a commitment to sound Safety, Health and Environmental (SHE) performance and says it has been investing heavily in process automation for increased safety and reduction of the human-error element.
- The Company was not part of the top 1,000 listed companies by market capitalisation as on March 31, 2026, and was therefore not required to prepare or submit a Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report for FY2025-26 — so no BRSR ESG metrics or targets are disclosed.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company discloses no named capacity-expansion or capex project in this report. Its only disclosed manufacturing footprint is the Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh facility, with installed module manufacturing capacity of 1.3 GW per annum, operating multiple automated production lines equipped with stringing, layup, lamination, framing and testing equipment. The Board's Report offers only a general statement that robust capital resources support long-term investments in expansion and technology upgrades, and that the Company aims to maintain sufficient cash and cash equivalents and may explore loan arrangements for working capital requirements; no project, quantum or timeline is named. The Company also states it has invested heavily in process automation for increased safety and reduction of human error.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's solar capacity is expected to nearly quadruple by 2035, providing sustained growth potential across the value chain
- Rooftop solar adoption is accelerating among residential and commercial users, expanding the distributed segment alongside utility-scale growth
- The ALMM policy is directing procurement toward domestically manufactured components, benefiting domestic manufacturers and integrators
- Demand is tilting toward higher-efficiency formats, with bifacial panels and perovskite technology moving to mainstream adoption faster than anticipated
- Hybrid solar projects paired with storage are becoming more prevalent, addressing intermittency
- Operating margins have improved on the back of stronger order flow, despite volatility in polysilicon, aluminium and copper prices
- Cell prices, a key input, remain vulnerable to fluctuations that can affect profitability; competition and technology pace can pressure pricing and market share
- Management attributes the step-up in the Company's operating performance to the Company having become fully operational during the year
- The Company is also securing orders from developers of power projects
- Operating margins have improved on the back of stronger order flow
- Customer advances against orders bolster liquidity
- Pass-through clauses are embedded in most orders, alongside order-backed procurement practices
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

Capital expenditure will be funded through a mix of existing cash reserves, internal accruals and sanctioned debt facilities.

The Company is evaluating alternative financing options such as factoring or supply chain financing to reduce reliance on borrowings, alongside tighter inventory management and improved receivables collection to shorten the working capital cycle.
